1	# Lab-DEBUG — Subsystem Design Document
2	
3	```text
4	Owner:        Hande (coordinator, DEBUG RTL)      Reviewer: Eren, Ömer
5	Stage / manual: Lab-DEBUG — docs/manuals/Lab-DEBUG_Assignment.pdf (DBG)
6	Status:       DRAFT (v0.1, 2026-09-26) — to be REVIEWED before any RTL is written
7	Requirements: REQ-DEBUG-001…020, REQ-IF-001…003, REQ-IF-005…007, REQ-PERF-001/002, REQ-VER-002
8	AI-assisted:  yes — Claude Opus 5.5 (claude.ai chat, 2026-09-26); log ID to be assigned (next free: AI-0004)
9	```
10	
11	Sources used: `REQUIREMENTS.md` §1.2, `INTERFACES.md` §1–3 and §6, `DECISIONS.md` (DEC-005/006/007/010/011/012/018),
12	`TEST_PLAN.md` §1–3, `ASSUMPTIONS.md` (006–009, 011), TA answers Q-02…Q-07 (`docs/meetings/INSTRUCTOR_QUESTIONS.md`).
13	Items marked **DESIGN CHOICE** are decided in this document and need reviewer approval; items marked
14	**TO VERIFY** are open until a test or datasheet confirms them.
15	
16	## 1. Purpose
17	
18	Lab-DEBUG is a transmit-only UART that reads 2^N 32-bit words from the read-only port of any on-chip
19	memory and streams them to MATLAB through the Basys-3 FT2232HQ USB-UART bridge, framed by a start word
20	(`0x55AACC03`) and an end word (`0xAA5503CC`). It is the observation tool for every later lab
21	(REQ-DEBUG-018), so its interface must stay stable once released.
22	
23	Scope boundaries:
24	
25	- Inside Lab-DEBUG: word/frame FSM, address counter, memory-latency handling, UART byte transmitter.
26	- **Not** inside Lab-DEBUG (belongs to the demo top level, owner Eren): button synchroniser/debounce/
27	  one-pulse for `start_in`, reset synchroniser (DEC-007), the ROM IP, pin constraints.
28	
29	## 2. Inputs
30	
31	| Port | Width | Type/format | Description |
32	|---|---|---|---|
33	| `clock_in` | 1 | std_logic | 100 MHz Basys-3 oscillator (REQ-IF-005) |
34	| `reset_in` | 1 | std_logic, active high | Synchronous reset of all registers; already synchronised in the top level (DEC-007) |
35	| `start_in` | 1 | std_logic, active high | Single-cycle pulse; starts one transfer **only** when idle (REQ-DEBUG-013, REQ-IF-007) |
36	| `mem_data_in` | 32 | std_logic_vector(31 downto 0) | Data from the memory read port; raw 32-bit container, no numeric meaning (INTERFACES §6) |
37	
38	## 3. Outputs
39	
40	| Port | Width | Type/format | Description |
41	|---|---|---|---|
42	| `mem_addr_out` | N | std_logic_vector(N-1 downto 0), unsigned | Read address, registered, held stable while a word is being sent |
43	| `txd_out` | 1 | std_logic | UART serial output, 8N1, idle = '1' (REQ-DEBUG-008) |
44	| `ready_out` | 1 | std_logic, active high | '1' = idle, '0' = transfer in progress (REQ-DEBUG-014, REQ-IF-006); registered |
45	
46	Generics (DEC-012, INTERFACES §3.2):
47	
48	| Generic | Default | Purpose |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| `N` | 14 | Address width → 2^N words. Declared first, named literally `N`, used for every address width and counter (TA Q-07). Valid range N ≥ 1 |
51	| `G_CLK_FREQ_HZ` | 100_000_000 | Clock frequency |
52	| `G_BAUD_RATE` | 1_000_000 | Baud rate (DEC-005); simulation overrides it to shorten run-time |
53	| `G_MEM_LATENCY` | 2 | Clock cycles from address register update to valid `mem_data_in`. See §12 for why 2 is the safe default |
54	
55	Derived constant: `C_CLKS_PER_BIT = (G_CLK_FREQ_HZ + G_BAUD_RATE/2) / G_BAUD_RATE` (rounded; = 100 for
56	the hardware configuration, 0 % error). An `assert C_CLKS_PER_BIT >= 4` guards against simulation settings
57	that are too fast for the FSM overhead.
58	
59	## 4. Clock
60	
61	Single clock domain, `clock_in` = 100 MHz (DEC-006). The bit timing is generated by a counter inside
62	`uart_tx` (clock-enable style); no derived clocks, no PLL/MMCM. Timing closure at 100 MHz is trivial for
63	this logic (small counters and a 32-bit shift register) — confirm WNS > 0 after implementation.
64	
65	## 5. Reset
66	
67	- `reset_in`: active high, **synchronous** in every clocked process (DEC-007). Synchronisation of the
68	  board button (BTNC, U18) is done in the top level, not here.
69	- Reset state: FSM = `S_IDLE`, `ready_out` = '1' (REQ-IF-006), `txd_out` = '1' (line idle),
70	  `mem_addr_out` = 0, UART transmitter idle.
71	- Reset during a transfer aborts it immediately. The PC then receives a short/truncated stream, which the
72	  MATLAB receiver must report as an error (fixed-length read with timeout, DEC-010 / REQ-SW-003). The next
73	  `start_in` produces a complete, correct frame (TB-DEBUG-06, HW-DEBUG-05).
74	- If `reset_in` and `start_in` are high in the same cycle, reset wins.
75	
76	## 6. Algorithm
77	
78	```text
79	on start_in = '1' while idle:
80	    ready_out <= '0'
81	    send_word(0x55AACC03)                       -- REQ-DEBUG-005
82	    for k in 0 .. 2^N - 1:                      -- REQ-DEBUG-004
83	        mem_addr_out <= k
84	        wait G_MEM_LATENCY cycles               -- REQ-DEBUG-019
85	        send_word(mem_data_in)
86	    send_word(0xAA5503CC)                       -- REQ-DEBUG-006
87	    ready_out <= '1'
88	
89	send_word(w):  for byte in [w(31:24), w(23:16), w(15:8), w(7:0)]:   -- MSB byte first (REQ-DEBUG-007, TA Q-02)
90	                   uart_send(byte)              -- 8N1, LSB bit first (REQ-DEBUG-008)
91	```
92	
93	The payload is sent unchanged even if it contains the delimiter values; the PC relies on the fixed
94	length `8 + 4·2^N` bytes, not on searching for the end word (DEC-010, TB-DEBUG-08).
95	
96	## 7. Internal architecture (block diagram)
97	
98	Two entities, one per file (CONTRIBUTING §6):
99	
100	| File | Entity | Content |
101	|---|---|---|
102	| `fpga/rtl/debug/uart_tx.vhd` | `uart_tx` | One-byte 8N1 transmitter with internal bit-period counter |
103	| `fpga/rtl/debug/debug.vhd` | `debug` | Lab-DEBUG top: word/frame FSM, address counter, latency wait, instantiates `uart_tx` |
104	
105	```text
106	                        debug (Lab-DEBUG)
107	            +-----------------------------------------------------------+
108	 start_in ->|                                                           |
109	 reset_in ->|   +-----------------------------+        +-------------+  |
110	 clock_in ->|   |  word / frame FSM           |tx_start|  uart_tx    |  |-> txd_out
111	            |   |  - phase: HDR / DATA / END  |------->|             |  |
112	            |   |  - byte_cnt  (0..3)         |tx_data |  shift_reg  |  |
113	            |   |  - lat_cnt   (0..L)         |==8===> |  clk_cnt    |  |
114	            |   |  - word_reg  (32-bit shift) |tx_done |  bit_cnt    |  |
115	            |   |  - addr_reg  (N-bit)        |<-------|             |  |
116	            |   +-----------------------------+        +-------------+  |
117	            |        |  ready_reg        ^  mem_data_in (32)            |
118	            +--------|-------------------|------------------------------+
119	                     v                   |
120	  ready_out <--------+     mem_addr_out (N) --> [ memory read port ] --+
121	                                              (ROM IP in the demo, any RAM port-B later)
122	```
123	
124	Internal signals between the FSM and `uart_tx` (DESIGN CHOICE):
125	
126	| Signal | Dir (FSM view) | Description |
127	|---|---|---|
128	| `tx_start` | out | '1' for exactly one cycle while FSM is in `S_SEND_BYTE`; `uart_tx` accepts it only when idle |
129	| `tx_data` | out | `word_reg(31 downto 24)` — the most significant byte of the shift register |
130	| `tx_done` | in | One-cycle pulse from `uart_tx` after the stop bit has lasted a full bit period |
131	
132	## 8. State machine (diagram + state table)
133	
134	One clocked process, enumerated state type, explicit `when others => state <= S_IDLE` (CONTRIBUTING §6).
135	A separate `phase` register (HDR / DATA / END) avoids three copies of the byte-sending states.
136	
137	```mermaid
138	stateDiagram-v2
139	    [*] --> S_IDLE : reset_in
140	    S_IDLE --> S_SEND_BYTE : start_in = 1 (load start word)
141	    S_SEND_BYTE --> S_WAIT_BYTE : tx_start for 1 cycle
142	    S_WAIT_BYTE --> S_SEND_BYTE : tx_done, byte_cnt below 3 (shift 8)
143	    S_WAIT_BYTE --> S_NEXT_WORD : tx_done, byte_cnt = 3
144	    S_NEXT_WORD --> S_MEM_WAIT : phase HDR (addr stays 0)
145	    S_NEXT_WORD --> S_MEM_WAIT : phase DATA, not last (addr + 1)
146	    S_NEXT_WORD --> S_SEND_BYTE : phase DATA, last (load end word)
147	    S_NEXT_WORD --> S_IDLE : phase END (ready = 1)
148	    S_MEM_WAIT --> S_SEND_BYTE : lat_cnt = L (capture mem_data_in)
149	```
150	
151	| State | Outputs / actions | Exit condition → next state |
152	|---|---|---|
153	| `S_IDLE` | `ready_reg` = '1'; `tx_start` = '0'; `start_in` is only looked at here (REQ-IF-007) | `start_in` = '1': load start word, `byte_cnt` ← 0, `addr_reg` ← 0, `phase` ← HDR, `ready_reg` ← '0' → `S_SEND_BYTE` |
154	| `S_SEND_BYTE` | `tx_start` = '1', `tx_data` = `word_reg(31:24)` (one cycle) | always → `S_WAIT_BYTE` |
155	| `S_WAIT_BYTE` | wait for the UART | `tx_done` and `byte_cnt` /= 3: `word_reg` ← `word_reg(23:0) & x"00"`, `byte_cnt` + 1 → `S_SEND_BYTE`; `tx_done` and `byte_cnt` = 3 → `S_NEXT_WORD` |
156	| `S_NEXT_WORD` | decide what the next word is; `byte_cnt` ← 0, `lat_cnt` ← 0 | HDR: `phase` ← DATA → `S_MEM_WAIT` · DATA, addr ≠ last: `addr_reg` + 1 → `S_MEM_WAIT` · DATA, addr = last: load end word, `phase` ← END → `S_SEND_BYTE` · END: `ready_reg` ← '1' → `S_IDLE` |
157	| `S_MEM_WAIT` | hold `addr_reg`; count `lat_cnt` | `lat_cnt` = `G_MEM_LATENCY`: `word_reg` ← `mem_data_in` → `S_SEND_BYTE`; else `lat_cnt` + 1 |
158	
159	"Last address" is detected as `addr_reg = (others => '1')`, so the address counter never needs N+1 bits
160	and never leaves the range 0 … 2^N−1 (TB-DEBUG-04). After the transfer the address stays at 2^N−1 until
161	the next start (DESIGN CHOICE — harmless, the memory is read-only).
162	
163	`uart_tx` internal FSM (DESIGN CHOICE): two states, `IDLE` / `SENDING`, a 10-bit shift register loaded
164	with `'1' & data & '0'` (stop, data, start), a `clk_cnt` 0 … `C_CLKS_PER_BIT`−1 and a `bit_cnt` 0 … 9.
165	`txd_out` is a register (glitch-free line). `busy` is not exported to the FSM; the FSM only issues
166	`tx_start` after `tx_done`, so the transmitter is always idle when a start arrives.
167	
168	## 9. Timing (waveform sketch, cycle counts)
169	
170	Notation: C = `C_CLKS_PER_BIT` (100 in hardware), L = `G_MEM_LATENCY`. Cycle counts are the **design
171	intent** and are measured in simulation (TB-DEBUG-02, TB-UART-02/03) — TO VERIFY.
172	
173	Handshake (REQ-DEBUG-013/014, INTERFACES §2):
174	
175	```text
176	clock_in   _|‾|_|‾|_|‾|_|‾|_|‾|_ ... _|‾|_|‾|_|‾|_
177	start_in   __|‾‾‾|__________________________________    sampled '1' at edge E_s
178	ready_out  ‾‾‾‾‾‾|_____________________ ... ___|‾‾‾‾‾   '0' right after E_s; '1' two edges after the last stop bit ends
179	txd_out    ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾|__start__|b0|b1|...                 start bit of byte 0x55 begins one edge after E_s
180	```
181	
182	- `ready_out` falls at the **same edge that samples `start_in` = '1'**, i.e. one clock after `start_in`
183	  rose. This matches the manual waveform and TB-DEBUG-02; it refines the PROPOSED wording in
184	  INTERFACES §2 ("first rising edge after the edge that sampled start") — reviewers please align the
185	  wording in INTERFACES.md.
186	- One UART byte: start bit + 8 data bits + stop bit, each exactly C clocks → 10·C clocks on the line.
187	- Gap between bytes of the same word: the FSM needs 2 extra clocks (`tx_done` → `S_SEND_BYTE` →
188	  accepted), so the stop bit is effectively C + 2 clocks long. Stop bit ≥ 1 bit period is guaranteed
189	  (TB-UART-03).
190	- Gap between data words: L + 2 extra clocks (`S_NEXT_WORD`, address update, L-cycle wait).
191	
192	Memory read timing (L = 1 shown; the address is held constant for the whole word):
193	
194	```text
195	edge          D+1            D+2             D+3
196	S_NEXT_WORD → addr_reg <= k  S_MEM_WAIT      S_MEM_WAIT: lat_cnt = 1 = L → word_reg <= mem_data_in
197	BRAM (L=1)                   samples addr k  mem_data_in = M[k] valid after D+2 → captured at D+3 ✔
198	BRAM (L=2)                   samples addr k  output reg loads at D+3 → valid after D+3 → captured at D+4 (lat_cnt = 2) ✔
199	```
200	
201	## 10. Data format
202	
203	| Field | Bytes on the wire, in order |
204	|---|---|
205	| Start word | `0x55`, `0xAA`, `0xCC`, `0x03` |
206	| Data word k (k = 0 … 2^N−1, from address k) | `W[31:24]`, `W[23:16]`, `W[15:8]`, `W[7:0]` |
207	| End word | `0xAA`, `0x55`, `0x03`, `0xCC` |
208	
209	Each byte: start bit '0', D0 … D7 (LSB first), stop bit '1', no parity (8N1). Total bytes per transfer
210	`8 + 4·2^N` (N = 14 → 65 544 bytes). Words narrower than 32 bits are zero-padded in the MSBs by the
211	**producer** (REQ-DEBUG-020); Lab-DEBUG does not interpret the data.
212	
213	## 11. Fixed-point representation
214	
215	Not applicable — Lab-DEBUG moves bytes and does no arithmetic on data. `mem_data_in` is a raw 32-bit
216	container and `mem_addr_out` an unsigned N-bit counter; both are already registered in INTERFACES §6.
217	No update needed there.
218	
219	## 12. Memory requirements
220	
221	Lab-DEBUG itself contains **no memory** (registers only). The demo memory lives in the top level:
222	
223	| Item | Value | Status |
224	|---|---|---|
225	| Demo ROM | Block Memory Generator, Single Port ROM, 2^14 × 32 bit (512 Kbit), always enabled, COE-initialised | REQ-DEBUG-016 |
226	| BRAM usage | 16 × RAMB36 of 50 on XC7A35T (32 %) — expected, read the IP summary | TO VERIFY |
227	| Read latency | 1 cycle without, 2 cycles with the primitive output register | ASSUMPTION-011, TO VERIFY in IP *Summary* tab |
228	
229	**Why `G_MEM_LATENCY` defaults to 2:** because `addr_reg` is held constant during `S_MEM_WAIT`,
230	waiting *longer* than the real latency is always safe (the data simply stays valid), while waiting
231	*shorter* captures the previous word — the classic "shifted by one" bug. The cost of one extra cycle per
232	word is 16 384 cycles ≈ 0.16 ms per transfer, negligible. Set the generic to the value from the IP summary
233	anyway and record it here; TB-DEBUG-07 runs L = 1 and L = 2.
234	
235	Integration note for later labs: the memory enable (`ena`/`enb`) must be tied to '1' or kept high while
236	Lab-DEBUG is reading, otherwise the output does not update.
237	
238	## 13. Latency
239	
240	| Event | Cycles (design intent) |
241	|---|---|
242	| `start_in` sampled → `ready_out` = '0' | 0 (same edge) |
243	| `start_in` sampled → first start bit on `txd_out` | 1 |
244	| Last stop bit finished → `ready_out` = '1' | 2 |
245	| Address update → data captured | L + 1 |
246	
247	## 14. Throughput
248	
249	Total clocks per transfer ≈ `(8 + 4·2^N)·(10·C + 2) + 2^N·(L + 2)`.
250	
251	| Configuration | Clocks | Time |
252	|---|---|---|
253	| Hardware: N = 14, C = 100, L = 2 | ≈ 65 544·1 002 + 16 384·4 ≈ 65.74 M | ≈ 0.657 s |
254	| Simulation: N = 3, C = 10, L = 2 | ≈ 40·102 + 8·4 = 4 112 | ≈ 41 µs |
255	
256	Line utilisation ≈ 1000 / 1002 = 99.8 % of the raw 1 Mbaud rate. No flow control: the FT2232HQ buffer
257	and the PC must keep up — ASSUMPTION-009, verified in HW-DEBUG-01/03.
258	
259	## 15. Interface protocol
260	
261	- **start/ready:** as INTERFACES §2 and §9 above. `start_in` pulses during a transfer are ignored because
262	  `start_in` is only evaluated in `S_IDLE` (REQ-IF-007, TB-DEBUG-05). `start_in` must be a one-cycle
263	  pulse: a level still high when the FSM returns to `S_IDLE` would start a second transfer. Producing
264	  the pulse is the job of the top-level button conditioning (Eren).
265	- **Memory read port:** Lab-DEBUG drives `mem_addr_out` and samples `mem_data_in` L cycles later
266	  (§9). It never writes. While a transfer is running it owns the read port; sharing that port with the
267	  next functional block is decided at Lab-ADC (DEC-009).
268	- **UART:** FPGA `txd_out` → pin A18 → FT2232HQ RXD (REQ-DEBUG-010; pin from INTERFACES §1.1, still to be
269	  checked against `Basys3_Master.xdc`).
270	
271	## 16. Resource estimate
272	
273	Estimate before synthesis — replace with post-synthesis numbers.
274	
275	| Resource | Estimate | Basis |
276	|---|---|---|
277	| FF | ≈ 70–90 | addr N=14, word_reg 32, byte/lat/phase/state ≈ 8, ready 1; uart: shift 10, clk_cnt 7, bit_cnt 4, misc 3 |
278	| LUT | < 100 | counters, comparators, byte mux |
279	| BRAM | 0 (DEBUG) + 16 RAMB36 (demo ROM) | §12 |
280	| DSP | 0 | no arithmetic |
281	
282	## 17. Verification method
283	
284	Testbench infrastructure (TEST_PLAN §1): behavioural UART receiver model in `fpga/tb/common/` that
285	samples `txd_out` in the middle of each bit and checks start/stop bits; a memory model with a generic
286	latency L returning a known pattern; self-checking output `Expected / Actual / PASS|FAIL` and a final
287	`TB_RESULT` line (DEC-011). Simulation uses N = 3 and C = 10 except TB-UART-02 (real C = 100).
288	
289	| ID | File | What it proves | REQ |
290	|---|---|---|---|
291	| TB-UART-01…03 | `fpga/tb/debug/tb_uart_tx.vhd` | 8N1 framing, LSB first, exact bit period (100 clocks), back-to-back bytes | DEBUG-008/009, PERF-001 |
292	| TB-DEBUG-01…09 | `fpga/tb/debug/tb_debug.vhd` | reset state, handshake timing, full frame, address order, start while busy, reset mid-transfer, L = 1/2, delimiter values in payload, two consecutive transfers | DEBUG-004…007/012…014/019, IF-006/007 |
293	| TB-TOPDBG-01 | Eren's top-level TB | button pulse → one frame; ROM content = COE | DEBUG-016 |
294	| MT-DEBUG-01…04 | MATLAB (Ömer) | decode, delimiter-in-payload, error on short stream, COE round trip | DEBUG-015, SW-003 |
295	| HW-DEBUG-01…05 | Basys-3 | terminal bring-up at 1 Mbaud, full ROM dump 0 mismatches, 10× repeat ≈ 0.66 s, button abuse, reset mid-transfer | DEBUG-008…017, PERF-002 |
296	
297	Demo evidence (REQ-VER-002): waveform screenshots showing `start_in`, `ready_out`, `txd_out` with at
298	least the start word and one data word decoded, plus the `TB_RESULT` lines.
299	
300	Recommended build order (DBG §3 "build progressively"): `uart_tx` + TB-UART → HW-DEBUG-01 with a
301	constant byte → `debug` FSM + TB-DEBUG → demo top level + ROM.
302	
303	## 18. Known limitations
304	
305	- Transmit only, no flow control, no parity, fixed 8N1 (REQ-DEBUG-002).
306	- A transfer cannot be paused; reset is the only way to abort it.
307	- `start_in` must be a clean one-cycle pulse (see §15).
308	- **1 000 000 baud is not yet verified on hardware** (ASSUMPTION-009), and the TA answered "No" to Q-06;
309	  the team's interpretation is recorded in DEC-005. Fallback: set `G_BAUD_RATE` = 115 200
310	  (C = 868, +0.006 % error), re-run TB-UART-02 — no other change needed.
311	- The design assumes the memory output is stable while the address is unchanged (true for Block
312	  Memory Generator ROM/RAM read ports with enable = '1').

# Lab-DEBUG — Subsystem Design Document

```text
Owner:        Hande (coordinator, DEBUG RTL)      Reviewer: Eren, Ömer
Stage / manual: Lab-DEBUG — docs/manuals/Lab-DEBUG_Assignment.pdf (DBG)
Status:       DRAFT (v0.1, 2026-09-26) — to be REVIEWED before any RTL is written
Requirements: REQ-DEBUG-001…020, REQ-IF-001…003, REQ-IF-005…007, REQ-PERF-001/002, REQ-VER-002
AI-assisted:  yes — Claude Opus 5.5 (claude.ai chat, 2026-09-26); log ID to be assigned (next free: AI-0004)
```

Sources used: `REQUIREMENTS.md` §1.2, `INTERFACES.md` §1–3 and §6, `DECISIONS.md` (DEC-005/006/007/010/011/012/018),
`TEST_PLAN.md` §1–3, `ASSUMPTIONS.md` (006–009, 011), TA answers Q-02…Q-07 (`docs/meetings/INSTRUCTOR_QUESTIONS.md`).
Items marked **DESIGN CHOICE** are decided in this document and need reviewer approval; items marked
**TO VERIFY** are open until a test or datasheet confirms them.

## 1. Purpose

Lab-DEBUG is a transmit-only UART that reads 2^N 32-bit words from the read-only port of any on-chip
memory and streams them to MATLAB through the Basys-3 FT2232HQ USB-UART bridge, framed by a start word
(`0x55AACC03`) and an end word (`0xAA5503CC`). It is the observation tool for every later lab
(REQ-DEBUG-018), so its interface must stay stable once released.

Scope boundaries:

- Inside Lab-DEBUG: word/frame FSM, address counter, memory-latency handling, UART byte transmitter.
- **Not** inside Lab-DEBUG (belongs to the demo top level, owner Eren): button synchroniser/debounce/
  one-pulse for `start_in`, reset synchroniser (DEC-007), the ROM IP, pin constraints.

## 2. Inputs

| Port | Width | Type/format | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clock_in` | 1 | std_logic | 100 MHz Basys-3 oscillator (REQ-IF-005) |
| `reset_in` | 1 | std_logic, active high | Synchronous reset of all registers; already synchronised in the top level (DEC-007) |
| `start_in` | 1 | std_logic, active high | Single-cycle pulse; starts one transfer **only** when idle (REQ-DEBUG-013, REQ-IF-007) |
| `mem_data_in` | 32 | std_logic_vector(31 downto 0) | Data from the memory read port; raw 32-bit container, no numeric meaning (INTERFACES §6) |

## 3. Outputs

| Port | Width | Type/format | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mem_addr_out` | N | std_logic_vector(N-1 downto 0), unsigned | Read address, registered, held stable while a word is being sent |
| `txd_out` | 1 | std_logic | UART serial output, 8N1, idle = '1' (REQ-DEBUG-008) |
| `ready_out` | 1 | std_logic, active high | '1' = idle, '0' = transfer in progress (REQ-DEBUG-014, REQ-IF-006); registered |

Generics (DEC-012, INTERFACES §3.2):

| Generic | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | 14 | Address width → 2^N words. Declared first, named literally `N`, used for every address width and counter (TA Q-07). Valid range N ≥ 1 |
| `G_CLK_FREQ_HZ` | 100_000_000 | Clock frequency |
| `G_BAUD_RATE` | 1_000_000 | Baud rate (DEC-005); simulation overrides it to shorten run-time |
| `G_MEM_LATENCY` | 2 | Clock cycles from address register update to valid `mem_data_in`. See §12 for why 2 is the safe default |

Derived constant: `C_CLKS_PER_BIT = (G_CLK_FREQ_HZ + G_BAUD_RATE/2) / G_BAUD_RATE` (rounded; = 100 for
the hardware configuration, 0 % error). An `assert C_CLKS_PER_BIT >= 4` guards against simulation settings
that are too fast for the FSM overhead.

## 4. Clock

Single clock domain, `clock_in` = 100 MHz (DEC-006). The bit timing is generated by a counter inside
`uart_tx` (clock-enable style); no derived clocks, no PLL/MMCM. Timing closure at 100 MHz is trivial for
this logic (small counters and a 32-bit shift register) — confirm WNS > 0 after implementation.

## 5. Reset

- `reset_in`: active high, **synchronous** in every clocked process (DEC-007). Synchronisation of the
  board button (BTNC, U18) is done in the top level, not here.
- Reset state: FSM = `S_IDLE`, `ready_out` = '1' (REQ-IF-006), `txd_out` = '1' (line idle),
  `mem_addr_out` = 0, UART transmitter idle.
- Reset during a transfer aborts it immediately. The PC then receives a short/truncated stream, which the
  MATLAB receiver must report as an error (fixed-length read with timeout, DEC-010 / REQ-SW-003). The next
  `start_in` produces a complete, correct frame (TB-DEBUG-06, HW-DEBUG-05).
- If `reset_in` and `start_in` are high in the same cycle, reset wins.

## 6. Algorithm

```text
on start_in = '1' while idle:
    ready_out <= '0'
    send_word(0x55AACC03)                       -- REQ-DEBUG-005
    for k in 0 .. 2^N - 1:                      -- REQ-DEBUG-004
        mem_addr_out <= k
        wait G_MEM_LATENCY cycles               -- REQ-DEBUG-019
        send_word(mem_data_in)
    send_word(0xAA5503CC)                       -- REQ-DEBUG-006
    ready_out <= '1'

send_word(w):  for byte in [w(31:24), w(23:16), w(15:8), w(7:0)]:   -- MSB byte first (REQ-DEBUG-007, TA Q-02)
                   uart_send(byte)              -- 8N1, LSB bit first (REQ-DEBUG-008)
```

The payload is sent unchanged even if it contains the delimiter values; the PC relies on the fixed
length `8 + 4·2^N` bytes, not on searching for the end word (DEC-010, TB-DEBUG-08).

## 7. Internal architecture (block diagram)

Two entities, one per file (CONTRIBUTING §6):

| File | Entity | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `fpga/rtl/debug/uart_tx.vhd` | `uart_tx` | One-byte 8N1 transmitter with internal bit-period counter |
| `fpga/rtl/debug/debug.vhd` | `debug` | Lab-DEBUG top: word/frame FSM, address counter, latency wait, instantiates `uart_tx` |

```text
                        debug (Lab-DEBUG)
            +-----------------------------------------------------------+
 start_in ->|                                                           |
 reset_in ->|   +-----------------------------+        +-------------+  |
 clock_in ->|   |  word / frame FSM           |tx_start|  uart_tx    |  |-> txd_out
            |   |  - phase: HDR / DATA / END  |------->|             |  |
            |   |  - byte_cnt  (0..3)         |tx_data |  shift_reg  |  |
            |   |  - lat_cnt   (0..L)         |==8===> |  clk_cnt    |  |
            |   |  - word_reg  (32-bit shift) |tx_done |  bit_cnt    |  |
            |   |  - addr_reg  (N-bit)        |<-------|             |  |
            |   +-----------------------------+        +-------------+  |
            |        |  ready_reg        ^  mem_data_in (32)            |
            +--------|-------------------|------------------------------+
                     v                   |
  ready_out <--------+     mem_addr_out (N) --> [ memory read port ] --+
                                              (ROM IP in the demo, any RAM port-B later)
```

Internal signals between the FSM and `uart_tx` (DESIGN CHOICE):

| Signal | Dir (FSM view) | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `tx_start` | out | '1' for exactly one cycle while FSM is in `S_SEND_BYTE`; `uart_tx` accepts it only when idle |
| `tx_data` | out | `word_reg(31 downto 24)` — the most significant byte of the shift register |
| `tx_done` | in | One-cycle pulse from `uart_tx` after the stop bit has lasted a full bit period |

## 8. State machine (diagram + state table)

One clocked process, enumerated state type, explicit `when others => state <= S_IDLE` (CONTRIBUTING §6).
A separate `phase` register (HDR / DATA / END) avoids three copies of the byte-sending states.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> S_IDLE : reset_in
    S_IDLE --> S_SEND_BYTE : start_in = 1 (load start word)
    S_SEND_BYTE --> S_WAIT_BYTE : tx_start for 1 cycle
    S_WAIT_BYTE --> S_SEND_BYTE : tx_done, byte_cnt below 3 (shift 8)
    S_WAIT_BYTE --> S_NEXT_WORD : tx_done, byte_cnt = 3
    S_NEXT_WORD --> S_MEM_WAIT : phase HDR (addr stays 0)
    S_NEXT_WORD --> S_MEM_WAIT : phase DATA, not last (addr + 1)
    S_NEXT_WORD --> S_SEND_BYTE : phase DATA, last (load end word)
    S_NEXT_WORD --> S_IDLE : phase END (ready = 1)
    S_MEM_WAIT --> S_SEND_BYTE : lat_cnt = L (capture mem_data_in)
```

| State | Outputs / actions | Exit condition → next state |
|---|---|---|
| `S_IDLE` | `ready_reg` = '1'; `tx_start` = '0'; `start_in` is only looked at here (REQ-IF-007) | `start_in` = '1': load start word, `byte_cnt` ← 0, `addr_reg` ← 0, `phase` ← HDR, `ready_reg` ← '0' → `S_SEND_BYTE` |
| `S_SEND_BYTE` | `tx_start` = '1', `tx_data` = `word_reg(31:24)` (one cycle) | always → `S_WAIT_BYTE` |
| `S_WAIT_BYTE` | wait for the UART | `tx_done` and `byte_cnt` /= 3: `word_reg` ← `word_reg(23:0) & x"00"`, `byte_cnt` + 1 → `S_SEND_BYTE`; `tx_done` and `byte_cnt` = 3 → `S_NEXT_WORD` |
| `S_NEXT_WORD` | decide what the next word is; `byte_cnt` ← 0, `lat_cnt` ← 0 | HDR: `phase` ← DATA → `S_MEM_WAIT` · DATA, addr ≠ last: `addr_reg` + 1 → `S_MEM_WAIT` · DATA, addr = last: load end word, `phase` ← END → `S_SEND_BYTE` · END: `ready_reg` ← '1' → `S_IDLE` |
| `S_MEM_WAIT` | hold `addr_reg`; count `lat_cnt` | `lat_cnt` = `G_MEM_LATENCY`: `word_reg` ← `mem_data_in` → `S_SEND_BYTE`; else `lat_cnt` + 1 |

"Last address" is detected as `addr_reg = (others => '1')`, so the address counter never needs N+1 bits
and never leaves the range 0 … 2^N−1 (TB-DEBUG-04). After the transfer the address stays at 2^N−1 until
the next start (DESIGN CHOICE — harmless, the memory is read-only).

`uart_tx` internal FSM (DESIGN CHOICE): two states, `IDLE` / `SENDING`, a 10-bit shift register loaded
with `'1' & data & '0'` (stop, data, start), a `clk_cnt` 0 … `C_CLKS_PER_BIT`−1 and a `bit_cnt` 0 … 9.
`txd_out` is a register (glitch-free line). `busy` is not exported to the FSM; the FSM only issues
`tx_start` after `tx_done`, so the transmitter is always idle when a start arrives.

## 9. Timing (waveform sketch, cycle counts)

Notation: C = `C_CLKS_PER_BIT` (100 in hardware), L = `G_MEM_LATENCY`. Cycle counts are the **design
intent** and are measured in simulation (TB-DEBUG-02, TB-UART-02/03) — TO VERIFY.

Handshake (REQ-DEBUG-013/014, INTERFACES §2):

```text
clock_in   _|‾|_|‾|_|‾|_|‾|_|‾|_ ... _|‾|_|‾|_|‾|_
start_in   __|‾‾‾|__________________________________    sampled '1' at edge E_s
ready_out  ‾‾‾‾‾‾|_____________________ ... ___|‾‾‾‾‾   '0' right after E_s; '1' two edges after the last stop bit ends
txd_out    ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾|__start__|b0|b1|...                 start bit of byte 0x55 begins one edge after E_s
```

- `ready_out` falls at the **same edge that samples `start_in` = '1'**, i.e. one clock after `start_in`
  rose. This matches the manual waveform and TB-DEBUG-02; it refines the PROPOSED wording in
  INTERFACES §2 ("first rising edge after the edge that sampled start") — reviewers please align the
  wording in INTERFACES.md.
- One UART byte: start bit + 8 data bits + stop bit, each exactly C clocks → 10·C clocks on the line.
- Gap between bytes of the same word: the FSM needs 2 extra clocks (`tx_done` → `S_SEND_BYTE` →
  accepted), so the stop bit is effectively C + 2 clocks long. Stop bit ≥ 1 bit period is guaranteed
  (TB-UART-03).
- Gap between data words: L + 2 extra clocks (`S_NEXT_WORD`, address update, L-cycle wait).

Memory read timing (L = 1 shown; the address is held constant for the whole word):

```text
edge          D+1            D+2             D+3
S_NEXT_WORD → addr_reg <= k  S_MEM_WAIT      S_MEM_WAIT: lat_cnt = 1 = L → word_reg <= mem_data_in
BRAM (L=1)                   samples addr k  mem_data_in = M[k] valid after D+2 → captured at D+3 ✔
BRAM (L=2)                   samples addr k  output reg loads at D+3 → valid after D+3 → captured at D+4 (lat_cnt = 2) ✔
```

## 10. Data format

| Field | Bytes on the wire, in order |
|---|---|
| Start word | `0x55`, `0xAA`, `0xCC`, `0x03` |
| Data word k (k = 0 … 2^N−1, from address k) | `W[31:24]`, `W[23:16]`, `W[15:8]`, `W[7:0]` |
| End word | `0xAA`, `0x55`, `0x03`, `0xCC` |

Each byte: start bit '0', D0 … D7 (LSB first), stop bit '1', no parity (8N1). Total bytes per transfer
`8 + 4·2^N` (N = 14 → 65 544 bytes). Words narrower than 32 bits are zero-padded in the MSBs by the
**producer** (REQ-DEBUG-020); Lab-DEBUG does not interpret the data.

## 11. Fixed-point representation

Not applicable — Lab-DEBUG moves bytes and does no arithmetic on data. `mem_data_in` is a raw 32-bit
container and `mem_addr_out` an unsigned N-bit counter; both are already registered in INTERFACES §6.
No update needed there.

## 12. Memory requirements

Lab-DEBUG itself contains **no memory** (registers only). The demo memory lives in the top level:

| Item | Value | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Demo ROM | Block Memory Generator, Single Port ROM, 2^14 × 32 bit (512 Kbit), always enabled, COE-initialised | REQ-DEBUG-016 |
| BRAM usage | 16 × RAMB36 of 50 on XC7A35T (32 %) — expected, read the IP summary | TO VERIFY |
| Read latency | 1 cycle without, 2 cycles with the primitive output register | ASSUMPTION-011, TO VERIFY in IP *Summary* tab |

**Why `G_MEM_LATENCY` defaults to 2:** because `addr_reg` is held constant during `S_MEM_WAIT`,
waiting *longer* than the real latency is always safe (the data simply stays valid), while waiting
*shorter* captures the previous word — the classic "shifted by one" bug. The cost of one extra cycle per
word is 16 384 cycles ≈ 0.16 ms per transfer, negligible. Set the generic to the value from the IP summary
anyway and record it here; TB-DEBUG-07 runs L = 1 and L = 2.

Integration note for later labs: the memory enable (`ena`/`enb`) must be tied to '1' or kept high while
Lab-DEBUG is reading, otherwise the output does not update.

## 13. Latency

| Event | Cycles (design intent) |
|---|---|
| `start_in` sampled → `ready_out` = '0' | 0 (same edge) |
| `start_in` sampled → first start bit on `txd_out` | 1 |
| Last stop bit finished → `ready_out` = '1' | 2 |
| Address update → data captured | L + 1 |

## 14. Throughput

Total clocks per transfer ≈ `(8 + 4·2^N)·(10·C + 2) + 2^N·(L + 2)`.

| Configuration | Clocks | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Hardware: N = 14, C = 100, L = 2 | ≈ 65 544·1 002 + 16 384·4 ≈ 65.74 M | ≈ 0.657 s |
| Simulation: N = 3, C = 10, L = 2 | ≈ 40·102 + 8·4 = 4 112 | ≈ 41 µs |

Line utilisation ≈ 1000 / 1002 = 99.8 % of the raw 1 Mbaud rate. No flow control: the FT2232HQ buffer
and the PC must keep up — ASSUMPTION-009, verified in HW-DEBUG-01/03.

## 15. Interface protocol

- **start/ready:** as INTERFACES §2 and §9 above. `start_in` pulses during a transfer are ignored because
  `start_in` is only evaluated in `S_IDLE` (REQ-IF-007, TB-DEBUG-05). `start_in` must be a one-cycle
  pulse: a level still high when the FSM returns to `S_IDLE` would start a second transfer. Producing
  the pulse is the job of the top-level button conditioning (Eren).
- **Memory read port:** Lab-DEBUG drives `mem_addr_out` and samples `mem_data_in` L cycles later
  (§9). It never writes. While a transfer is running it owns the read port; sharing that port with the
  next functional block is decided at Lab-ADC (DEC-009).
- **UART:** FPGA `txd_out` → pin A18 → FT2232HQ RXD (REQ-DEBUG-010; pin from INTERFACES §1.1, still to be
  checked against `Basys3_Master.xdc`).

## 16. Resource estimate

Estimate before synthesis — replace with post-synthesis numbers.

| Resource | Estimate | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| FF | ≈ 70–90 | addr N=14, word_reg 32, byte/lat/phase/state ≈ 8, ready 1; uart: shift 10, clk_cnt 7, bit_cnt 4, misc 3 |
| LUT | < 100 | counters, comparators, byte mux |
| BRAM | 0 (DEBUG) + 16 RAMB36 (demo ROM) | §12 |
| DSP | 0 | no arithmetic |

## 17. Verification method

Testbench infrastructure (TEST_PLAN §1): behavioural UART receiver model in `fpga/tb/common/` that
samples `txd_out` in the middle of each bit and checks start/stop bits; a memory model with a generic
latency L returning a known pattern; self-checking output `Expected / Actual / PASS|FAIL` and a final
`TB_RESULT` line (DEC-011). Simulation uses N = 3 and C = 10 except TB-UART-02 (real C = 100).

| ID | File | What it proves | REQ |
|---|---|---|---|
| TB-UART-01…03 | `fpga/tb/debug/tb_uart_tx.vhd` | 8N1 framing, LSB first, exact bit period (100 clocks), back-to-back bytes | DEBUG-008/009, PERF-001 |
| TB-DEBUG-01…09 | `fpga/tb/debug/tb_debug.vhd` | reset state, handshake timing, full frame, address order, start while busy, reset mid-transfer, L = 1/2, delimiter values in payload, two consecutive transfers | DEBUG-004…007/012…014/019, IF-006/007 |
| TB-TOPDBG-01 | Eren's top-level TB | button pulse → one frame; ROM content = COE | DEBUG-016 |
| MT-DEBUG-01…04 | MATLAB (Ömer) | decode, delimiter-in-payload, error on short stream, COE round trip | DEBUG-015, SW-003 |
| HW-DEBUG-01…05 | Basys-3 | terminal bring-up at 1 Mbaud, full ROM dump 0 mismatches, 10× repeat ≈ 0.66 s, button abuse, reset mid-transfer | DEBUG-008…017, PERF-002 |

Demo evidence (REQ-VER-002): waveform screenshots showing `start_in`, `ready_out`, `txd_out` with at
least the start word and one data word decoded, plus the `TB_RESULT` lines.

Recommended build order (DBG §3 "build progressively"): `uart_tx` + TB-UART → HW-DEBUG-01 with a
constant byte → `debug` FSM + TB-DEBUG → demo top level + ROM.

## 18. Known limitations

- Transmit only, no flow control, no parity, fixed 8N1 (REQ-DEBUG-002).
- A transfer cannot be paused; reset is the only way to abort it.
- `start_in` must be a clean one-cycle pulse (see §15).
- **1 000 000 baud is not yet verified on hardware** (ASSUMPTION-009), and the TA answered "No" to Q-06;
  the team's interpretation is recorded in DEC-005. Fallback: set `G_BAUD_RATE` = 115 200
  (C = 868, +0.006 % error), re-run TB-UART-02 — no other change needed.
- The design assumes the memory output is stable while the address is unchanged (true for Block
  Memory Generator ROM/RAM read ports with enable = '1').

## 19. Change history

| Version | Date | Author | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | 2026-09-26 | Hande (AI-assisted, Claude Opus 5.5) | First draft for review |

## PR #3 Review: well aligned with our specs, with 4 fixes to make before merge

The PR contains only the Lab-DEBUG design doc (`docs/architecture/subsystems/debug.md`, v0.1). The RTL and testbenches aren't in yet. It is based on the current `main` (PR #1 and #2 merged) and has no merge conflicts. I found **no technical defect that should block merging**. Two of the problems are actually in *our* docs, not in Hande's.

### What matches the specs
| Area | Check |
|---|---|
| Port names | `reset_in`, `clock_in`, `start_in`, `mem_addr_out`, `mem_data_in`, `txd_out`, `ready_out` all match REQ-DEBUG-011 ✓ |
| Parameters | `N` named literally with default 14 (TA Q-07, DEC-012) ✓. `G_BAUD_RATE` = 1 000 000 (DEC-005) ✓ |
| Frame | Start word 55AACC03, end word AA5503CC, bytes sent MSB first (TA Q-02), 8N1 with LSB first, fixed length `8 + 4·2^N` bytes (DEC-010) ✓ |
| Handshake | `ready_out` = 1 after reset (REQ-IF-006). `start_in` is only read in the idle state, so pulses during a transfer are ignored (REQ-IF-007) ✓ |
| Reset | Synchronous; the button synchroniser lives in the top level (DEC-007). A reset in the middle of a transfer aborts it cleanly ✓ |
| Memory latency | Address is held constant while waiting a fixed L cycles, default L = 2. I checked the timing sketch: data is captured correctly for both L=1 and L=2 ✓. Last semester's design uses the same fixed-wait method (`READ_WAIT_CYCLES = 4`), which is consistent with DEC-018 |
| Address range | Last address detected as all 1's, so the counter never goes out of range ✓ |
| Coding rules | One entity per file (`uart_tx`, `debug`), enumerated FSM with `when others`, all outputs registered ✓ |
| Numbers | I recomputed them: 1 Mbaud gives 100 clocks per bit; a full N=14 transfer is ≈ 65.74 M cycles = **0.657 s**; simulation with N=3, C=10 is 4 112 cycles; the ROM uses 16 BRAM36 ✓ |
| Test plan | Test IDs match TEST_PLAN, the checks are self-checking with a `TB_RESULT` line, and demo evidence is planned ✓ |

### Fixes before merge
1. **INTERFACES §2 has the wrong handshake wording. This is my error, not Hande's.** I wrote that `ready_out` goes low "from the first rising edge *after* the edge that sampled `start_in`". That describes a response delayed by one more cycle. The manual's waveform shows `ready_out` falling at the same edge that samples `start_in` = 1, and Hande's §9 does exactly that. Fix INTERFACES in this PR and log it as CORR-0002.
2. **INTERFACES §3.2:** the `G_MEM_LATENCY` default there says "from IP summary (1 or 2)". Change it to **2** to match the design doc. Her reasoning holds: waiting longer than the real latency is safe, waiting shorter shifts every word by one.
3. **PR scope doesn't match our workflow.** The title says "design, RTL and testbenches" and the body says "Draft PR collecting all Lab-DEBUG work", but the PR isn't marked as draft. TEAM_MANUAL §4 says the design doc is reviewed and **merged before any RTL** is written, and PRs stay small. With Wednesday's deadline, I'd do this:
   - rename this PR to the design doc only and merge it after review;
   - put `uart_tx` + TB-UART in one new PR, and the `debug` FSM + TB-DEBUG in another.

   Otherwise one large PR is left to review on Tuesday night.
4. **AI records are incomplete.**
   - There is no AI-0004 row in `ai/AI_USAGE_LOG.md`, and the document header still says "log ID to be assigned".
   - Hande used **claude.ai chat**, a different interface from ours, so it needs a new row in `ai/TOOLS_AND_MODELS.md`.
   - The chat export should go into `ai/sessions/`.

   Hande's PR says these will be added later. They are syllabus requirements, so they should land before merge.

Minor: §18 still describes 1 Mbaud as uncertain because of the TA's "No". DEC-005 is ACCEPTED, so that sentence should read as a plan B only.

### Not blocking, but still to verify later
- The ROM IP's actual latency, from the IP's Summary tab (ASSUMPTION-011).
- 1 Mbaud on real hardware (HW-DEBUG-01).
- **A dependency on your part:** `start_in` must be a clean one-cycle pulse. If the button signal is still high when the FSM returns to idle, a second transfer starts. Your button-conditioning block must guarantee this, and TB-TOPDBG-01 should test it.

I can post this review as a comment on PR #3 from your GitHub account; I won't approve it on your behalf, since that approval should be yours. I can also fix fixes 1–2 in INTERFACES myself and add the CORR-0002 record, on a small separate branch or pushed to Hande's branch, whichever she prefers. Should I do either?

# CORR-0002 — Wrong `ready_out` timing wording in INTERFACES §2

```text
Date:            2026-09-26        Member: eeerenbuyukbas (review of PR #3)   Related AI record: AI-0001 (origin), AI-0005 (fix)
File(s):         INTERFACES.md §2, TEST_PLAN.md TB-DEBUG-02
Found by:        review — Hande's design document (debug.md §9, AI-0004) pointed out the mismatch
```

## What the AI produced (AI-0001)
"`ready_out` is low from the first rising edge after the edge that sampled `start_in` = '1'
(i.e. registered, 1-cycle response)."

## What was wrong
Read literally, this delays `ready_out` by one extra clock: the register would be cleared one edge
*after* the sampling edge. The manual waveforms (DBG §1, CTRL §1) show `ready_out` falling when
`start_in` falls, i.e. at the edge that samples `start_in` = '1'. A registered FSM naturally does this.
The text contradicted its own parenthesis ("registered, 1-cycle response").

## How it was detected
Design review: `debug.md` §9 derived the timing from the manual waveform and flagged the difference.

## Correction applied
INTERFACES §2 now states that `ready_out` is cleared at the same rising edge that samples
`start_in` = '1' (low one clock after `start_in` rose). TEST_PLAN TB-DEBUG-02 wording aligned.

## Verification of the correction
Pending — TB-DEBUG-02 must check the exact cycle once the RTL exists.

## Lesson
Describe handshake timing by naming the edge ("the edge that samples X") and check it against the
manual waveform, not by prose alone.

# CORR-0002 — Wrong `ready_out` timing wording in INTERFACES §2

```text
Date:            2026-09-26        Member: eeerenbuyukbas (review of PR #3)   Related AI record: AI-0001 (origin), AI-0005 (fix)
File(s):         INTERFACES.md §2, TEST_PLAN.md TB-DEBUG-02
Found by:        review — Hande's design document (debug.md §9, AI-0004) pointed out the mismatch
```

## What the AI produced (AI-0001)
"`ready_out` is low from the first rising edge after the edge that sampled `start_in` = '1'
(i.e. registered, 1-cycle response)."

## What was wrong
Read literally, this delays `ready_out` by one extra clock: the register would be cleared one edge
*after* the sampling edge. The manual waveforms (DBG §1, CTRL §1) show `ready_out` falling when
`start_in` falls, i.e. at the edge that samples `start_in` = '1'. A registered FSM naturally does this.
The text contradicted its own parenthesis ("registered, 1-cycle response").

## How it was detected
Design review: `debug.md` §9 derived the timing from the manual waveform and flagged the difference.

## Correction applied
INTERFACES §2 now states that `ready_out` is cleared at the same rising edge that samples
`start_in` = '1' (low one clock after `start_in` rose). TEST_PLAN TB-DEBUG-02 wording aligned.

## Verification of the correction
Pending — TB-DEBUG-02 must check the exact cycle once the RTL exists.

## Lesson
Describe handshake timing by naming the edge ("the edge that samples X") and check it against the
manual waveform, not by prose alone.

content.text:
Squash-merge is now the only merge method, merged branches are deleted automatically, and the 3 old branches are gone. **I didn't convert the merge commit into a squash commit**, even though it's technically possible.

**Settings in place:**
- **Merge methods:** only **Squash and merge** is allowed. "Create a merge commit" and "Rebase" buttons no longer appear on PRs.
- **Squash commit title:** taken from the PR title (e.g. `docs(debug): ... (#3)`).
- **Branch auto-delete:** turned on. A branch is deleted automatically as soon as its PR is merged.

**Deleted branches:**
- `feature/debug-design`: its commits were already in `main`, so I deleted it directly.
- `docs/team-manual` and `docs/ta-answers-2026-09-26`: these were squash-merged, so their original commits aren't in `main` under the same hashes. Before deleting I checked that each branch's content is **identical** to its squash commit in `main`. Nothing was lost.
- I also deleted the 3 local copies. The repo now has only `main`, and there are no open PRs.

**Why I left the merge commit alone:**
- **Force-push required:** rewriting it means force-pushing to `main`. That requires switching off branch protection first, which I'd have to turn back on afterwards.
- **Teammates' copies diverge:** everyone's local `main` would drift from GitHub. Hande's starting RTL now, and if she has already branched from `main` she'd hit conflicts.
- **References break:** the review comment and the AI-0005 record point to commit `4ceb9e2`, which would disappear from `main`'s history.
- **The gain is cosmetic:** the file contents are identical either way. The only difference is two extra commits plus one merge commit in the history.

With the new settings this can't happen again. If you still want the rewrite, tell me and I'll do it after telling the team; everyone would then need to re-sync their local `main`.

Otomatik silme kapatıldı. Merge edilen branch'ler artık silinmeden kalacak. Squash-merge dışındaki merge yöntemleri kapalı kalmaya devam ediyor.

Silinen bir branch'e geri dönmek gerekirse zaten iki yol var:

- **PR sayfasından geri yükleme:** merge edilmiş bir PR'ın sayfasında **"Restore branch"** butonu çıkar. Bugün sildiğimiz 3 branch de PR #1, #2 ve #3'ün sayfalarından tek tıkla geri gelir; GitHub commit'leri silmez.
- **`main` geçmişinden geri dönme:** squash commit'lerin her biri `main`'de duruyor. Bir değişikliği geri almak gerekirse `git revert` ile yeni bir PR açılır; bunun için branch'in var olması gerekmez.

Bir yan etkisi var: merge sonrası eski branch'ler birikecek. Ara sıra "şu branch'leri temizle" derseniz, silmeden önce içeriklerinin `main`'de olduğunu bugünkü gibi kontrol edip öyle silerim.

=== BODY
## What changed
UART byte transmitter (`uart_tx`) and its self-checking testbench, as designed in
`docs/architecture/subsystems/debug.md` §7–§9 (v0.2).

## Why
First RTL block of Lab-DEBUG (demo Wed Sep 30). The word/frame FSM (`debug.vhd`) builds on it.

## Related Requirements
REQ-DEBUG-002, REQ-DEBUG-008, REQ-DEBUG-009, REQ-PERF-001

## Files changed
- `fpga/rtl/debug/uart_tx.vhd` (new)
- `fpga/tb/debug/tb_uart_tx.vhd` (new)

## Simulation performed
`tb_uart_tx`, Vivado 2025.2 XSim (also cross-checked with GHDL 4.1, VHDL-93 and -2008).
Two DUT instances: G_CLKS_PER_BIT = 10 (TB-UART-01, -03) and 100 = real 1 Mbaud divider (TB-UART-02).

## Testbench result
TB_RESULT: PASS (37/37 checks)
- TB-UART-01: 0x55/0x00/0xFF/0x81 — start bit, data LSB first, stop bit, 1-cycle done, idle line
- TB-UART-02: every bit period = 100 clocks, frame = 1000 clocks (0 % baud error)
- TB-UART-03: back-to-back bytes correct, stop bit = 12 clocks (C + 2, as in debug.md §9)
Testbench sensitivity checked by injecting 3 bugs (wrong bit order, wrong divider, wrong stop bit): all detected.

## Synthesis result
Not yet (sub-block; synthesised with the Lab-DEBUG top).

## Hardware result
Not applicable yet: HW-DEBUG-01 needs a data-capable USB cable (current cable is power-only).

## AI usage
AI-0004 — RTL and testbench drafted with Claude Opus 5.5 (claude.ai chat), simulated and reviewed by Hande.

## Known limitations
- Log file not yet stored in `simulation/results/` (DEC-011) — will be added.
- `b_done` stays '1' at the very end of the waveform because the testbench stops the clock; not a DUT issue.

## Reviewer checklist
- [ ] Functionality matches the requirement(s) and the subsystem design doc
- [ ] Synthesizable; no latches; no gated/derived clocks; async inputs synchronised
- [ ] Reset behaviour defined for every register
- [ ] Timing: met at 100 MHz (or not affected)
- [ ] Numerical accuracy / fixed-point formats as documented in INTERFACES.md §6
- [ ] Interface compatibility (ports, widths, signedness, handshake, latency) — dependants updated
- [ ] Testbench really checks the requirement (self-checking, corner cases, reset)
- [ ] No magic numbers; generics/constants used
- [ ] Docs updated (REQUIREMENTS status, TRACEABILITY_MATRIX, HANDOFF, PROJECT_STATUS)
- [ ] I can explain this code without the author present

## PR #4: kodda sorun yok, merge'den önce 3 küçük düzeltme gerekiyor

PR'da sadece `uart_tx` ve testbench'i var; `debug` FSM'i henüz eklenmemiş. Hande'nin "PASS" raporuna güvenmek yerine iki şeyi kendim tekrarladım:

| Kontrol | Sonuç |
|---|---|
| Simülasyon (Vivado **2023.2** XSim) | `TB_RESULT: PASS (37/37)`. Bit süresi 100 clock, frame 1000 clock, iki byte arasındaki stop bit 12 clock (tasarım dokümanındaki C+2 değeri) ✓ |
| Sentez (XC7A35T, sadece bu blok) | Hata ve latch yok. 23 LUT, 22 flip-flop. 100 MHz'de zamanlama payı **+6,7 ns** ✓ |
| Tasarım dokümanına uyum | 8N1 çerçeve ve LSB-first gönderim doğru. Meşgulken gelen `start` yok sayılıyor, çıkış registerlı, reset senkron. `done` pulse'u tek cycle ✓ |
| Kodlama kuralları | Sihirli sayı yok (`C_LAST_BIT` sabit olarak tanımlı), `when others` var, başlıkta gereksinim ve AI kaydı var ✓ |
| Testbench | Kendini kontrol ediyor. TB-UART-02 gerçek bölen değeriyle (100) bit süresini tam clock sayısı olarak ölçüyor. Hande ayrıca 3 bilinçli hata ekleyip testbench'in bunları yakaladığını da göstermiş ✓ |

**Merge'den önce düzeltilmesi gerekenler:**
1. **Başlık ve kapsam:** başlık "uart_tx, debug FSM" diyor ama PR'da sadece `uart_tx` var. Başlık `uart_tx`'e göre düzeltilip PR merge edilebilir; `debug` FSM'i yeni bir PR'la gelsin.
2. **Simülasyon logu eksik:** DEC-011'e göre `simulation/results/debug/` altına konması gerekiyor. Hande de bunu eksik olarak yazmış.
3. **AI-0004 kayıt dosyası ve claude.ai sohbet dışa aktarımı hâlâ yok.** PR #3'ten beri bekliyor.

İsterseniz bu bulguları PR #4'e yorum olarak yazarım.

### ⚠️ Bugün karar verilmesi gereken bir konu: Vivado sürümü
Hande **Vivado 2025.2** kullanıyor; sizin bilgisayarınızda **2023.2** var ve DEC-008 tek sürümde anlaşmayı öngörüyordu.

- Salt VHDL kodunda bu sorun değil; 2023.2'de de sorunsuz çalıştı.
- Ama Ömer'in oluşturacağı **ROM IP'si (`.xci`) sürüme bağlı.** 2025.2'de oluşturulan bir IP, 2023.2'de açılamaz.
- Önerim: **lab PC'sindeki sürümü öğrenin ve üçünüz de onu kullanın.** Karar, Ömer ROM IP'sini oluşturmadan önce verilmeli.

## Kendiniz test etmek için
Kendi bilgisayarınızda, repo klasöründe (PowerShell veya Git Bash):

**1. PR'ın branch'ine geçin:**
```bash
gh pr checkout 4
```

**2. Derleyin, elaborate edin ve çalıştırın:**
```bash
C:/Xilinx/Vivado/2023.2/bin/xvhdl.bat fpga/rtl/debug/uart_tx.vhd fpga/tb/debug/tb_uart_tx.vhd
```
```bash
C:/Xilinx/Vivado/2023.2/bin/xelab.bat -debug typical tb_uart_tx -s tb_uart_tx_sim
```
```bash
C:/Xilinx/Vivado/2023.2/bin/xsim.bat tb_uart_tx_sim -R
```
Çıktının sonunda `TB_RESULT: PASS (37/37 checks)` görmelisiniz. Oluşan `xsim.dir`, `*.log` ve `*.pb` dosyaları `.gitignore`'da, commit'e girmez.

**3. Dalga formunu görmek için** (demoda da gösterilecek):
```bash
C:/Xilinx/Vivado/2023.2/bin/xsim.bat tb_uart_tx_sim -gui
```
Açılan pencerede sinyalleri Waveform'a ekleyin: `a_txd`, `a_done`, `b_txd`, `b_done`. Sonra Tcl konsoluna `run all` yazın.

**4. İşiniz bitince `main`'e dönün:**
```bash
git switch main
```

Donanım testi şu an mümkün değil: bunun için top-level'ın (sizin paketiniz) yazılmış olması ve veri aktarabilen bir micro-USB kablosu gerekiyor. Hande'nin kablosu sadece şarj kablosu.

## Lab-DEBUG'ı bitirmek için eksikler
Bugün 26 Eylül, teslim 30 Eylül Çarşamba. `main`'de şu an sadece dokümanlar var. Açık PR'larda `uart_tx` dışında kod yok; sizden ve Ömer'den henüz hiçbir şey push edilmemiş.

| Kim | Eksik | Durum |
|---|---|---|
| **Hande** | `debug.vhd` (kelime ve çerçeve FSM'i). Testbench'i `tb_debug` ve TB-DEBUG-01…09. Testbench'lerde ortak kullanılacak UART alıcı modeli (`fpga/tb/common/`) | Başlanmadı |
| **Siz (Eren)** | `top_debug_demo.vhd`: reset senkronizörü; buton için senkronizör, debounce ve 1-cycle pulse; `debug` ve ROM bağlantısı; LD6 LED'i. Resmi `Basys3_Master.xdc`'den türetilmiş XDC. `create_debug_demo.tcl`. Top-level testbench'i TB-TOPDBG-01. Sentez, implementation ve bitstream | Başlanmadı |
| **Ömer** | ROM IP (16384×32, COE ile yüklenen; Summary sekmesindeki gecikme değeri kaydedilecek). COE üretici (başlangıç/bitiş kelimelerini de içeren test deseniyle). MATLAB alıcısı: 1 Mbaud, sabit uzunlukta 65 544 byte okuma, başlık kontrolü, çözme, COE ile karşılaştırma. MT-DEBUG-01…04 | Başlanmadı |
| **Hep birlikte** | Veri aktarabilen USB kablosu, FTDI sürücüsü. HW-DEBUG-01…05, 1 Mbaud'un gerçekten çalıştığının doğrulanması (R-15). Demo kanıtları: `start`, `ready` ve `txd` sinyallerini gösteren dalga formu ekran görüntüleri, loglar, `docs/verification/` raporları. PROJECT_STATUS kontrol listesi, HANDOFF, AI kayıtları, `lab-debug-demo` tag'i ve bitstream'li release | — |

**Kritik yol:** `debug.vhd`, top-level ve ROM IP → birleştirme simülasyonu → bitstream → donanım testi → Çarşamba demosu. Üç paketin de en geç Pazartesi akşamı PR olarak gelmesi gerekiyor. Salı günü sadece birleştirme ve donanım testi kalmalı.

Sizin paketiniz (top-level ve buton işleme) tek başına başlayabilir; `debug`'ın portları tasarım dokümanında sabitlendi. İsterseniz tasarımıyla şimdi başlayalım.
2025.2 yi indiriyorum. Hangisini kurmalıyım
[Image: source: C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-USER-OneDrive-Masa-st--EEE391-Project\8f5cb339-90a8-4d18-9b2b-0146cfd89092\images\1.png]

Bu ekranda **mutlaka düzeltmeniz gereken bir yer var: 7 Series seçili değil.** Basys-3'teki FPGA bir Artix-7 (XC7A35T). 7 Series seçilmezse Vivado bu kart için proje oluşturamaz ve bitstream üretemez.

**Design Tools**

| Seçenek | Seçim | Neden |
|---|---|---|
| Vivado | ✅ (zaten zorunlu) | Ana araç |
| Vitis HLS | ✅ (gri, değiştirilemiyor) | Vivado ile birlikte geliyor |
| Vitis Networking P4 | ❌ | Ağ donanımı için, bizim işimiz değil |
| **Vitis Model Composer** | **❌ kaldırın** | Simulink eklentisi; bize gerekmiyor, çok yer kaplıyor |
| Vitis Embedded Development | ❌ | MicroBlaze yazılım geliştirme için; projede işlemci yok |
| Power Design Manager | ❌ | Gerek yok |
| DocNav | ✅ isteğe bağlı | Xilinx dokümanlarını açar, küçük bir araç |

**Devices**
- **7 Series:** yanındaki **+**'ya basıp açın ve sadece **Artix-7**'yi işaretleyin. Kintex-7, Virtex-7 ve Spartan-7 gerekmiyor.
- Diğerlerinin hepsi (Alveo, Kria, SoCs, UltraScale, UltraScale+, Versal, Engineering Sample) **❌**.

**Installation Options**
- **Install Cable Drivers: ✅ kalsın.** Bitstream'i USB üzerinden karta yüklemek için gerekli. Kurulum sırasında Basys-3'ü bilgisayardan çıkarın.
- **Acquire or Manage a License Key: ❌ kaldırabilirsiniz.** ML Standard, XC7A35T için ücretsiz ve lisans istemiyor. İşaretli kalırsa kurulum sonunda gereksiz bir lisans penceresi açılır, zararı yok.

Bu seçimlerle indirme boyutu ve disk ihtiyacı ekranda gördüğünüz 9,25 GB / 40,1 GB'tan belirgin şekilde düşer. Seçimleri yaptıktan sonra alttaki "Download Size / Disk Space Required" değerleri güncellenir.

**Sonrası için:**
- 2023.2'yi kaldırmanız gerekmiyor, iki sürüm yan yana durabilir. Ama projeyi artık 2025.2 ile açın.
- **Ömer de 2025.2 kurmalı.** ROM IP'sini oluşturmadan önce bu şart, çünkü 2025.2'de oluşturulan IP 2023.2'de açılmaz. Lab PC'sindeki sürüm de kontrol edilmeli.
- Kurulum bitince DEC-008'i ("ekip Vivado 2025.2 kullanır") ve ASSUMPTION-004'ü güncelleyeyim mi? Bunu bir sonraki doküman PR'ına ekleyebilirim.

message.content:
2025.2 yi kurdum. Kendi kısmım için yapmam gereken şeylere başlayabiliriz. Hande bana şöyle bir mesaj attı: Eren top modülde bağlayacağın portlar: clock_in, reset_in, start_in (1 clock'luk pulse olmalı, debounce senin tarafta), mem_addr_out (N bit), mem_data_in (32 bit), txd_out (A18), ready_out (LD6). Generic varsayılanları donanıma göre ayarlı: N=14, 1 Mbaud, G_MEM_LATENCY=2.

İşlemlere başlayalım. Team manual'deki 6. sectiondaki gereklilikleri unutma. Ayrıca başlamadan önce Handenin son açık kalan PR ını da kontrol edebilirsin. Bir sorun yoksa ilerleyelim

- `simulation/results/2026-09-26_tb_uart_tx.log`, `simulation/results/2026-09-26_tb_debug.log` (new)

  `ai/outputs/2026-09-26_AI-0006_pr4-verification.md`, `ai/sessions/README.md`

## Simulation performed
Vivado 2025.2 XSim:
- GUI runs by Hande (behavioral simulation, `run all`)
- Independent batch-mode re-run (xvhdl / xelab / xsim) by Claude Code on Hande's PC (AI-0006)

Testbench settings:
- `tb_uart_tx`: G_CLKS_PER_BIT = 10 and 100 (real 1 Mbaud divider)
- `tb_debug`: N = 3 (8 words), 10 clocks/bit, three DUTs: latency 2/2, 1/1, and memory 1 with G_MEM_LATENCY = 2

## Testbench result
- `tb_uart_tx`: TB_RESULT: PASS (37/37 checks) — TB-UART-01…03
- `tb_debug`: TB_RESULT: PASS (97/97 checks) — TB-DEBUG-01…09
  - ready falls at the start sampling edge, rises 2 clocks after the last stop bit (debug.md §9)
  - payload containing 55AACC03 / AA5503CC / 00000000 / FFFFFFFF sent unchanged (DEC-010)
  - memory latency 1 and 2 correct; waiting longer than the real latency is safe (debug.md §12)

Logs: `simulation/results/2026-09-26_tb_*.log` (batch-mode run; machine-identifying lines redacted, repo is public).

AI-reported, not human-verified: a GHDL 4.1 cross-check (VHDL-93 and -2008), a GHDL synthesis check
(no latches) and mutation tests (3 injected bugs in uart_tx, 7 in debug — all detected) were run by the AI
in the claude.ai chat sandbox (AI-0004). No logs of these runs are in the repo.

## Synthesis result
Not yet in Vivado (will be done with the demo top level).

## Hardware result
Not applicable yet: HW-DEBUG-01…05 need the demo top level, ROM and a data-capable USB cable.

## AI usage
- AI-0004 — design doc, RTL and testbenches drafted with Claude Opus 5.5 (claude.ai chat); simulated and reviewed by Hande.
- AI-0006 — Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5): RTL review, batch simulation re-run, status documentation. No RTL changed.
- Session export of the claude.ai chat will be added to `ai/sessions/` after a personal-data check.

## Review findings (AI-0006, non-blocking — details in HANDOFF.md)
1. `uart_tx.vhd` has no `use ieee.numeric_std.all;` (not needed functionally).
2. Inner `case phase is` in `debug.vhd` has no `when others` (all values covered).
3. Byte slices (`31 downto 24`, `x"00"`) and the assert limit `4` could be named constants.
4. UART receiver model is inline in each testbench instead of `fpga/tb/common/` (deviation noted in TEST_PLAN).
5. TB-DEBUG-05 injects busy starts only while waiting for a byte; structurally safe (start only read in S_IDLE).

- `start_in` must be a clean 1-cycle pulse; button conditioning is in the top level (Eren).
- XSim advances to the 3 ms watchdog limit after the testbench finishes (no timeout message) — cosmetic.
- 1 Mbaud not yet verified on hardware (ASSUMPTION-009 → HW-DEBUG-01).

## Merge method
Squash-merge and delete the branch, as in DEC-004 / CONTRIBUTING §2.

lines: --- Purpose : One-byte UART transmitter, 8N1 (1 start bit, 8 data bits LSB first,
---           no parity, 1 stop bit). Sub-block of Lab-DEBUG.
--- AI      : AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5.5, claude.ai chat, 2026-09-26), AI-0004
---   * tx_start_in is sampled only in S_IDLE; pulses while sending are ignored.
---   * Every bit lasts exactly G_CLKS_PER_BIT clock cycles.
---   * tx_done_out is a one-cycle pulse after the stop bit has lasted a full
---     bit period; the transmitter is idle again in that same cycle.
---   * txd_out is a register (glitch-free line), '1' when idle and during reset.
-        reset_in    : in  std_logic;                     -- active high, synchronous
-        tx_data_in  : in  std_logic_vector(7 downto 0);  -- sampled with tx_start_in
-        txd_out     : out std_logic;                     -- serial line, idle '1'
-        tx_done_out : out std_logic                      -- 1-cycle pulse, frame finished
-    constant C_LAST_BIT : natural := 9;   -- bit index of the stop bit (0 = start bit)
-    -- frame shift register: (9) stop bit, (8 downto 1) data, (0) start bit
-    signal clk_cnt   : natural range 0 to G_CLKS_PER_BIT - 1 := 0;
-    signal bit_cnt   : natural range 0 to C_LAST_BIT := 0;
-                        if clk_cnt = G_CLKS_PER_BIT - 1 then  -- end of current bit
-                            if bit_cnt = C_LAST_BIT then      -- stop bit finished
-                                txd_reg   <= shift_reg(1);    -- next bit on the line
---             TB-UART-01  bytes 0x55, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x81: start bit, 8 data bits
---                         LSB first, stop bit, 1-cycle done pulse, idle line
---             TB-UART-02  real divider (100 clocks/bit): every bit period and
---                         the frame length measured in clock cycles
---             TB-UART-03  back-to-back bytes: correct data, stop bit >= 1 bit
--- Output  : one "Expected / Actual / PASS|FAIL" line per check and a final
--- Run     : Vivado "Run Behavioral Simulation", then "Run All" (or Tcl: run all)
--- AI      : AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5.5, claude.ai chat, 2026-09-26), AI-0004
-    constant C_FAST       : positive := 10;      -- short divider for TB-UART-01/03
-    constant C_REAL       : positive := 100;     -- hardware divider for TB-UART-02
-    function hex(v : std_logic_vector(7 downto 0)) return string is
-    clk <= not clk after C_CLK_PERIOD / 2 when not sim_done else '0';
-    -- stops a hanging simulation (e.g. no start bit ever appears)
-            report "TB_RESULT: FAIL (timeout - simulation did not finish)" severity failure;
-        type t_bytes is array (natural range <>) of std_logic_vector(7 downto 0);
-        constant C_TEST_BYTES : t_bytes(0 to 3) := (x"55", x"00", x"FF", x"81");
-        procedure check(name : string; ok : boolean; expected : string; actual : string) is
-                report name & "  Expected: " & expected & "  Actual: " & actual & "  PASS"

## 1. PR #4: no blocking issues, you can approve it

Hande's latest version includes the `debug` FSM, testbench logs, status updates and AI records. I independently re-ran it on the team's version, **Vivado 2025.2**:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tb_uart_tx` | **PASS 37/37** ✓ |
| `tb_debug` | **PASS 97/97** ✓ (all of TB-DEBUG-01…09 are present) |
| `debug.vhd` code review | Matches the design doc on all key points ✓ |
| Requirement statuses | Marked correctly ✓ |

**`debug.vhd` details checked:**
- `ready` drops at the edge that samples `start_in` and comes back up 2 clocks after the last stop bit.
- `start_in` is ignored while a transfer is running.
- Memory data is captured `L+1` edges after the address changes.
- Bytes go out MSB first; the last address is detected without an overflow bit.

**Requirement statuses:** Hande only moved requirements verified by simulation to VERIFIED. Items that need a hardware test are left as "NOT VERIFIED". That's the right way to do it.

**Not blocking:**
- `debug` hasn't been synthesized in Vivado yet. I couldn't do it here either (see the blocker below). Hande can run it on her PC in 2 minutes, or it can be done with your top level.
- The 6 minor findings listed in the PR (missing `numeric_std`, some literal byte widths, etc.) can wait until after the demo.
- The claude.ai chat export still needs to be added.

## ⚠️ Blocker: your Vivado can't target the Basys-3
Your 2025.2 install **only has Kintex-7 support, no Artix-7**. Simulation works because it needs no device, but synthesis, implementation and bitstream **can't target the Basys-3**. Also, 2023.2 is no longer on this PC.

**Fix:**
1. Open **"Add Design Tools or Devices for Vivado 2025.2"** from the Start menu (or Vivado → **Help → Add Design Tools or Devices**).
2. Under **7 Series**, select **Artix-7**.
3. Kintex-7 isn't needed; you can deselect it.

## 2. Your package: demo top level, plan
§6.1 applies here: I don't write code until you confirm the plan.

**PROJECT STATE SUMMARY:** Lab-DEBUG is due Wed Sep 30.
- `debug` + `uart_tx`: done and passing in simulation (PR #4).
- Top level (you) and ROM + MATLAB (Ömer): not started.
- **Pins confirmed against Digilent's official `Basys3_Master.xdc`:** W5 clock, U18 BTNC, T18 BTNU, A18 TX, U14 LD6. ASSUMPTION-003 is now verified.

**CURRENT OBJECTIVE:** The demo top level: buttons → `debug` → ROM → UART/LED, plus the XDC, Tcl script and testbenches.

**Design decisions I need you to confirm:**
1. **Debounce: we'd deviate from the reference design.**
   - Last semester's top level only synchronizes the start button and detects its rising edge; there's no debounce.
   - The problem: if you hold the button longer than the transfer (0.66 s), bouncing on release can start a **second transfer**.
   - Proposal: 2-FF synchronizer → **10 ms** debounce (as a generic) → 1-cycle pulse. This deviation from DEC-018 gets logged in DECISIONS.
2. **Reset:** BTNC through a 2-FF synchronizer (DEC-007). The reference uses the raw button signal directly.
3. **ROM (to agree with Ömer):**
   - IP name `rom_debug_demo`: Single-Port ROM, 16384×32, always enabled, output register on → latency 2, matching the `G_MEM_LATENCY=2` default.
   - Proposal: **generate the IP from the Tcl script (`create_ip`) instead of committing a `.xci`.** This removes the Vivado version dependency.
   - Ömer provides the COE file and the IP parameters.
4. **Simulating before the IP exists:** a behavioral ROM model with the same name goes in the testbench folder. Once Ömer's IP is in, the same test runs with the real IP.

input.content:
# Lab-DEBUG demo top level — Subsystem Design Document

```text
Owner:        Eren (top level)            Reviewer: Ömer (ROM/COE interface), Hande (debug interface)
Stage / manual: Lab-DEBUG — docs/manuals/Lab-DEBUG_Assignment.pdf (DBG §2 demo); TA Q-04, Q-05
Status:       DRAFT v0.1 (2026-09-26) — to be REVIEWED before RTL
Requirements: REQ-DEBUG-010, REQ-DEBUG-016, REQ-DEBUG-017, REQ-CTRL-006 (inputs), REQ-HW-002,
              REQ-IF-002 (start pulse), REQ-IF-006, REQ-VER-001
AI-assisted:  yes — Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 (AI-0007)
```

Sources: `debug.md` v0.2 (Lab-DEBUG block), `INTERFACES.md` §1.1 and §3, DEC-005/007/008/012/013/018,
TA Q-04/Q-05, Digilent `Basys-3-Master.xdc` (digilent-xdc commit `69d3501`, MIT), reference design
`Borek-32/…/rtl/top_module.vhd` (start-button handling only). **DESIGN CHOICE** = decided here, needs
reviewer approval. **TO VERIFY** = open until a test confirms it.

## 1. Purpose

Board-level wrapper for the Lab-DEBUG demonstration (DBG §2, TA Q-04): press **BTNU** → Lab-DEBUG reads
the whole 16 384 × 32 demo ROM and sends it to MATLAB at 1 Mbaud; **LD6** shows `ready`. Lab-CTRL is not
part of this demo (TA Q-04).

Inside this top level: reset synchroniser, start-button conditioning, Lab-DEBUG instance, ROM instance,
LED. Not inside: the UART/FSM logic (`debug`, Hande), the ROM content and the MATLAB receiver (Ömer).

## 2. Inputs

| Port | Width | Pin | Type/format | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clock_in` | 1 | W5 | 100 MHz oscillator | System clock (REQ-IF-005) |
| `reset_in` | 1 | U18 (BTNC) | raw push-button, active high, asynchronous | System reset (DEC-007, TA Q-05 → DEC-018) |
| `start_in` | 1 | T18 (BTNU) | raw push-button, active high, asynchronous, bouncing | Start one transfer |

## 3. Outputs

| Port | Width | Pin | Type/format | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `txd_out` | 1 | A18 | UART 8N1, 1 Mbaud, idle '1' | To FT2232HQ RXD (REQ-DEBUG-010) |
| `ready_out` | 1 | U14 (LD6) | '1' = LED on = idle | Lab-DEBUG `ready_out` (REQ-IF-006) |

All five pins verified against Digilent's official `Basys-3-Master.xdc` (2026-09-26) → ASSUMPTION-003 VERIFIED.

Generics (defaults = hardware; simulation overrides them):

| Generic | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | 14 | Address width, passed to `debug`. **Must equal the ROM address width (14) in hardware** |
| `G_CLK_FREQ_HZ` | 100_000_000 | Passed to `debug` |
| `G_BAUD_RATE` | 1_000_000 | Passed to `debug` (DEC-005) |
| `G_MEM_LATENCY` | 2 | Passed to `debug`; must be ≥ ROM latency (2, §12) |
| `G_DEBOUNCE_CYCLES` | 1_000_000 | Start-button stable time = 10 ms at 100 MHz (DEC-019) |

## 4. Clock

Single domain, `clock_in` 100 MHz, constrained with `create_clock -period 10.000` (XDC). No MMCM
(DEC-006). The ROM uses the same clock.

## 5. Reset

- `reset_in` (BTNC) → `sync_2ff` (two flip-flops, `ASYNC_REG`) → `rst` → `reset_in` of `debug` and of the
  button conditioner (DEC-007: synchronous use). The reference design feeds the raw button directly; we
  synchronise it (DEC-007 outranks DEC-018).
- Power-up: all registers have initial values (FPGA configuration loads them), so no extra power-on
  reset is needed. **DESIGN CHOICE:** the reset synchroniser initialises to '1', which additionally holds
  the design in reset for the first two clocks after configuration.
- Reset bounce is harmless (several resets in a row). No debounce on reset.
- The ROM has no reset (read-only).

## 6. Algorithm

```text
rst       = sync2(reset_in)
start_p   = rising_edge_pulse( debounce( sync2(start_in), G_DEBOUNCE_CYCLES ) )   -- exactly 1 clock
debug     : start_in <= start_p ; mem_data_in <= rom[mem_addr_out] (latency 2)
txd_out   = debug.txd_out ; ready_out = debug.ready_out
```

**Start-button conditioning (DESIGN CHOICE, DEC-019 — deviation from the reference design):**
the reference design only synchronises BTNU and detects its rising edge. Mechanical bounce (typically
< 5 ms) then produces several rising edges per press. During a transfer they are ignored (REQ-IF-007), but
if the button is held longer than one transfer (0.66 s), the bounce **on release** or a re-press bounce can
start a second, unwanted transfer. We therefore require the synchronised level to be stable for
`G_DEBOUNCE_CYCLES` (10 ms) before accepting it, and emit a pulse only on the debounced 0 → 1 change.

Debounce algorithm (counter-based, one clock domain):

```text
if sync_level = stable then cnt <= 0
elsif cnt = G_DEBOUNCE_CYCLES - 1 then stable <= sync_level; cnt <= 0
else cnt <= cnt + 1
pulse <= stable_new and not stable_old          -- registered, 1 clock
```

## 7. Internal architecture

| File | Entity | Content |
|---|---|---|

| Full transfer, N = 14 | ≈ 65.74 M cycles ≈ 0.657 s (debug.md §14) |
| Bounces shorter than 10 ms | produce **no** pulse |

## 10. Data format

Unchanged from `debug.md` §10: start word, 16 384 ROM words MSB byte first, end word → 65 544 bytes.

## 11. Fixed-point representation

Not applicable (no arithmetic).

## 12. Memory requirements — ROM interface (to agree with Ömer)

**DESIGN CHOICE (DEC-013 refinement):** the ROM IP is **generated by the Tcl script** with `create_ip`
instead of committing a version-specific `.xci`; only the COE file and the Tcl parameters are in git.

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| IP / component name | `rom_debug_demo` (Block Memory Generator) |
| Memory type | Single Port ROM, Native interface |
| Width × depth | 32 × 16 384 (address 14 bit) |
| Enable | Always enabled (no `ena` port) |
| Output register | Primitives output register ON → **read latency 2** (= `G_MEM_LATENCY` default) |
| Ports | `clka`, `addra(13:0)`, `douta(31:0)` |
| Init file | `fpga/ip/rom_debug_demo/debug_demo.coe` (radix 16) — **owner Ömer** |
| BRAM | 16 × RAMB36 of 50 (32 %) — TO VERIFY in the utilisation report |

**Demo test pattern (proposal for Ömer's COE generator):** word k (k = 0 … 16 383) is

| k | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `55AACC03` | start word inside the payload (DEC-010) |
| 1 | `AA5503CC` | end word inside the payload (DEC-010) |
| 2 | `00000000` | all zeros |
| 3 | `FFFFFFFF` | all ones |
| 4 … 35 | `1 << (k − 4)` | walking one over all 32 bits (byte-order and bit-order errors) |
| 36 … 16 383 | `(not k)[15:0] & k[15:0]` | unique per address → detects shifted/missing words |

The same formula is implemented in `fpga/tb/common/debug_demo_pattern_pkg.vhd` (simulation model and
testbench) and must be implemented in MATLAB (COE generator and hardware check), so simulation, COE and
hardware dump are all checked against one definition.

**Simulation before the IP exists:** `fpga/tb/debug/rom_debug_demo.vhd` is a behavioural model with the
same entity name and ports (latency 2, content from the pattern package). It is used only in the standalone
XSim flow and **must not be added to the Vivado project** (the IP provides the real model there).

## 13. Latency

See §9. ROM read latency 2; `debug` waits `G_MEM_LATENCY` = 2 (debug.md §12).

## 14. Throughput

Unchanged from `debug.md` §14 (≈ 0.657 s per transfer).

## 15. Interface protocol

- `start_p` is a clean 1-clock pulse, as required by `debug.md` §15 and REQ-IF-002.
- A press during a transfer is ignored by `debug` (REQ-IF-007); a press held through the end of a transfer
  does **not** start a new transfer (no new 0 → 1 debounced edge).
- **DESIGN CHOICE:** if BTNU is held while BTNC is released, the debounced level rises after reset and one
  transfer starts ≈ 10 ms later. Accepted (operator action, harmless).

## 16. Resource estimate

| Resource | Estimate | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| FF | ≈ 105 | debug 78 (synthesised), button 20-bit counter + 5, reset sync 2 |
| LUT | ≈ 110 | debug 79 (synthesised) + counter/compare |
| BRAM | 16 RAMB36 | ROM |
| DSP | 0 | |

## 17. Verification method

| ID | File | What it proves | REQ |
|---|---|---|---|
| TB-BTN-01 | `fpga/tb/debug/tb_button_conditioner.vhd` | clean press → exactly 1 pulse, 1 clock wide, after 2 + D + 1 cycles | IF-002 |
| TB-BTN-02 | same | press with bounce (glitches shorter than D) → exactly 1 pulse | IF-002 |
| TB-BTN-03 | same | release with bounce → 0 pulses; glitch while idle → 0 pulses | IF-002 |
| TB-BTN-04 | same | long hold → 1 pulse only | IF-002 |
| TB-BTN-05 | same | reset during a press → no pulse while in reset | DEC-007 |
| TB-TOPDBG-01 | `fpga/tb/debug/tb_top_debug_demo.vhd` | bouncing press → exactly one frame of `8 + 4·2^N` bytes; header, all words = pattern, footer; LED low during / high after | DEBUG-016 |
| TB-TOPDBG-02 | same | press held beyond the end of the transfer and released with bounce → no second frame | IF-007, DEC-019 |
| TB-TOPDBG-03 | same | second press → second identical frame | DEBUG-001 |
| SYN-TOPDBG | `fpga/vivado/create_debug_demo.tcl` | synthesis + implementation, timing met at 100 MHz, BRAM = 16, no critical warnings | REQ-VER-001 |
| HW-DEBUG-01…05 | TEST_PLAN §3 | on the board with Ömer's MATLAB receiver | DEBUG-008…017 |

- The ROM IP is fixed at 14 address bits; changing N requires regenerating the IP (Tcl parameter).

  feed synchronisers.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# create_debug_rom.tcl
# Purpose : (Re)create the Lab-DEBUG demo ROM IP "debug_rom" from debug_rom.coe:
#           Block Memory Generator, Single Port ROM, 16384 x 32 bit, always
#           enabled, primitive output register ON (read latency 2 clocks).
# Design  : docs/architecture/subsystems/debug.md §12 (demo ROM)
# Reqs    : REQ-DEBUG-016, REQ-DEBUG-019; ASSUMPTION-011; DEC-008 (Vivado 2025.2), DEC-013
# Author  : Ömer (omerkutlu1030)
# AI      : AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code desktop, 2026-09-26), AI-0007
#
# Usage (from the repository root):
#   vivado -mode batch -source fpga/ip/create_debug_rom.tcl
# Result:
#   fpga/ip/debug_rom/debug_rom.xci   (committed; generated products are git-ignored)
# Regenerate the COE first if the test pattern changes:
#   matlab -batch "addpath('matlab/debug'); generate_debug_coe('fpga/ip/debug_rom.coe', 14)"
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

set ip_name   debug_rom
set part      xc7a35tcpg236-1                 ;# Basys-3 (ASSUMPTION-001)
set addr_bits 14                              ;# N = 14 (REQ-DEBUG-016)
set data_bits 32

set ip_root [file normalize [file dirname [info script]]]
set coe     [file join $ip_root ${ip_name}.coe]
set ip_dir  [file join $ip_root $ip_name]

if {![file exists $coe]} {
    error "COE file not found: $coe (run generate_debug_coe in MATLAB first)"
}
if {[file exists $ip_dir]} {
    file delete -force $ip_dir                ;# start clean, the script is the source of truth
}

create_project -in_memory -part $part
create_ip -name blk_mem_gen -vendor xilinx.com -library ip \
          -module_name $ip_name -dir $ip_root

set_property -dict [list \
    CONFIG.Interface_Type                             {Native} \
    CONFIG.Memory_Type                                {Single_Port_ROM} \
    CONFIG.Write_Width_A                              $data_bits \
    CONFIG.Read_Width_A                               $data_bits \
    CONFIG.Write_Depth_A                              [expr {1 << $addr_bits}] \
    CONFIG.Enable_A                                   {Always_Enabled} \
    CONFIG.Register_PortA_Output_of_Memory_Primitives {true} \
    CONFIG.Use_RSTA_Pin                               {false} \
    CONFIG.Load_Init_File                             {true} \
    CONFIG.Coe_File                                   $coe \
] [get_ips $ip_name]

set ip [get_ips $ip_name]
puts "INFO: created [get_property IPDEF $ip] -> [get_property IP_FILE $ip]"
foreach p {Memory_Type Write_Depth_A Read_Width_A Enable_A Register_PortA_Output_of_Memory_Primitives Coe_File} {
    puts [format "INFO:   %-44s = %s" $p [get_property CONFIG.$p $ip]]
}
